canonical_topic: p-n junction doping for directional current flow
definition: Solar cells use doped semiconductor layers (p-type and n-type) to force freed electrons to flow in a consistent direction, producing usable current rather than random electron motion.
core_idea: A p-type layer (doped to be positively charged, missing electrons) is sandwiched with an n-type layer (doped with excess electrons); when sunlight frees an electron on the n-type side, it migrates toward the positive p-type side, creating a directional current.
key_points: P-type semiconductors are doped with atoms lacking electrons, giving a net positive charge.
N-type semiconductors are doped with atoms carrying excess electrons, giving a net negative charge.
Free electrons naturally move away from negative charge and toward positive charge, which the p-n sandwich exploits to generate consistent current.
relationships: Builds on the basic PV effect (band gap excitation) described alongside it.
